newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble firms on client demand, short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Rouble firms on client demand, short-covering.

text.p: The rouble firmed on Monday on bank client demand and short-covering and dealers said banks were also setting aside funds for Wednesday's sales of government securities.

On April 23 the Finance Ministry will auction 7.50 trillion roubles of 364-day GKO discount Treasury bills (series 23005) and 4.00 trillion roubles in an additional 707-day tranche of the two-year bonds maturing March 1999 (series 24011).
roubles/dollar Apr 21 midday Apr 21 early Apr 18 close
"Today's dollar decline seemed due to fufilling client orders," Inkombank dealer Vladislav Savelyev said.
Dealers said some banks were already raising funds for Wednesday's auctions, in anticipation of more expensive rouble credits on Tuesday as tomorrow/next rates were quoted at 30-35 percent.
"But given steady overnight rates, today's fall in dollar rates could be due, apart from client orders, to short-covering," Neftekhimbank dealer Vladimir Zrazhevsky said.
